title: MCP model-compatibility test catalog
description: Machine-readable definitions of the compatibility tests run against an MCP server / tool / live session per LLM model. See 03-compatibility-test-suite.md.

path_conventions.description: Namespaces used in measured.inputs and threshold.source paths.

user_facing_name.description: Names the CHECK, for a list of checks: 'Namespaced tool names stay within length limit'.

finding_name.description: Names the FINDING, for a list of problems: 'Namespaced tool names exceed the length limit'. A findings card that printed user_facing_name would read as though the check itself were the bad news.

level.description: the SUBJECT of the test (what it is about). environment = the whole multi-server setup.

scope.description: What the measurement and limit span. per_tool = one tool; per_server = one server's tool set in isolation (single-server upper bound); aggregate = ALL connected servers + built-in tools combined in one request/session (where caps like Claude 10k / OpenAI 128 / Cursor 40 actually bind). NOTE: most vendor caps are aggregate; there is no documented per-MCP-server hard tool cap.

data_phase.description: coarse: static (no execution) vs runtime (any execution). Superseded by execution_mode.

execution_mode.description: ACCESS required to run the test. static_connection = connected + tools/list, NO execution, NO source; single_tool_exec = one tools/call in isolation (tool playground); live_session = multi-turn monitored session (BACKLOG). Never requires server source code.

source.description: dataset path supplying the limit, or null when computed

fallback.description: value used when source is null/absent

computed.description: formula when the threshold is derived rather than read

warn_at.description: boundary that triggers warn (fraction or absolute)

rule.description: universal=all models; threshold_present=only if source field non-null; capability=requires a capability flag; client_configured=needs a target host; computed_fallback=universal via a derived threshold

extends_existing.description: link to an existing optimize.ts/scan_event check this generalizes

failure_mode.description: What concretely breaks when the test is non-compliant.

impact.description: The negative consequence of non-compliance (the 'what happens if it fails').

recoverability.description: hard_fail = does not work until fixed; soft_degrade = works but worse

model_severity.description: How severe non-compliance is PER MODEL. When variant=false the test's flat `severity` applies to all models. When variant=true the engine evaluates `rules` in order against the model's dataset entry; the first match yields the resolved severity + an evidence-backed rationale.

variant.description: does severity depend on the specific model?

default.description: severity when no rule matches (or when variant=false)

rules.description: ordered; first whose `when` predicate is true wins

when.description: predicate over model.* / cross.* (DSL: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, contains, exists/absent, && , ||). e.g. 'model.tools_mcp.max_tools_hard.value exists'

failure_mode.description: optional per-rule override of impact.failure_mode for this class of model

consequence.description: what happens specifically on this class of model

evidence_fields.description: dataset paths whose {value, source_url, source_tier, confidence} are attached as evidence for this verdict

rationale_template.description: human rationale; {placeholders} are filled from the model's provider name + evidence field values at resolve time
